newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus 96 profit about $450 mln - source.
newsitem.headline: Airbus 96 profit about $450 mln - source.

text.p: Europe's Airbus plane-making consortium posted an "operating surplus" of around $450 million for 1996, down from the prior year, a source close to the aircraft venture said on Wednesday.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa), Germany's partner in Airbus, earlier said the grouping made 707 million marks ($410 million) in net profit last year, down from 855 million marks in the prior year.
The Airbus 1997 profit is expected to fall again as it expects to deliver around 50 wide-body jets and 133 narrow-body jets this year. Margins are higher on wide-bodies.

An Airbus Industrie spokesman declined to confirm or deny the Dasa figures, saying: "We are not allowed by our partners to reveal the operating surplus we make." However, he did say that Airbus had been making surpluses since 1990.

Because of its French partnership structure as a "groupement d'interest economique" (GIE), Airbus does not publish financial accounts. It does not retain any operating surpluses -- its terminology for profits -- but passes these to its partners.
It makes provisions and reserves for currency risks and for directly-owned assets.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Dasa, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.

The source said Airbus receives revenues and draws up its accounts in dollars. The surplus in Airbus' books differed from the profit published in Dasa's annual report because the Germany company had translated the dollars into marks.

The partners receive income from Airbus in three streams -- money which goes back to repay the refundable launch aid lent by governments, payments for each partner's supply contracts with Airbus and finally the portion of the operating surplus due to each company as an Airbus shareholder.
The 1996 surplus was lower than 1995 due to the smaller number of wide-body jets sold in the total mix of aircraft. Pricing pressure in the market also cut into profit margins.
That pressure on margins also hit archrival Boeing, which last week reported disaappointing first quarter earnings, the source said.
The Airbus partners are in talks to change its status to an integrated limited liability company owning its own assets by 1999, in a bid to improve competitiveness. ($ = 1.723 German Marks)
